title: Docs + quickstart updates for onboarding checklist (Hosted API) with cross-language parity
creator: Wei Chen
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description:
Problem:
Customers are missing critical “production-safe” steps during Hosted API onboarding (timeouts/retries, streaming stability, quotas/budgets, model pinning, fallback/rollout, observability hooks). Support sees repeated tickets (401/403 API key mistakes, 429 surprises, streaming disconnect confusion, usage dashboard lag). Console will ship an in-product checklist; docs + quickstarts must become the canonical source for each checklist step and be consistent across Python/TypeScript/Go.

Scope (this ticket):
1) Add a canonical docs entry for the onboarding checklist (the doc people can share externally and Console deep-links into).
2) Update quickstarts and template code to mirror checklist steps and ensure parity across Python/TS/Go.
3) Add/validate redirects and IA changes so existing quickstarts resolve to the new structure without breaking inbound links.

Non-goals:
- Building the Console checklist UI or progress-tracking backend (see Console/Platform tickets).
- Fully guided in-product tours or automated remediation suggestions.
- Private/Dedicated onboarding wizards (future phases).

Primary stakeholders:
- Docs/DevEx: Elliot Price (docs lead), Wei Chen (Hosted API quickstarts), Jean-Paul Laurent (onboarding content)
- SDK: Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan (production defaults)
- Product: Nikhil Sharma / Marissa Cole
- Support: Dev Patel (macro + triage alignment)

Notes:
This work must align 1:1 with the checklist step definitions used by Console (step names, ordering, acceptance criteria). Any mismatch will create confusion and support load.
acceptance_criteria:
Docs:
- A public-facing “Onboarding checklist / First production launch checklist” page exists in docs and is linked from the Hosted API onboarding entry point.
- Each checklist step has: a short explanation, “why it matters”, common failure modes, and deep links to the relevant how-to pages.
- The checklist doc uses the final step names/copy (per content guidelines) and matches Console ordering.
- Redirects are in place for any moved/renamed pages referenced by existing quickstarts and external links.

Quickstarts:
- Python/TypeScript/Go quickstarts include consistent sections for: API key + env var setup, first request, streaming, retries/timeouts, handling 429/backoff, usage dashboard expectations (lag), quotas/budgets guidance, model pinning, fallback policy, observability hooks (request ID/logging).
- Code snippets compile/run and demonstrate “production-safe defaults” (timeouts/retries) without introducing breaking changes.
- A single source-of-truth mapping exists from checklist step → docs URL → quickstart section → example repo file.

Quality:
- Docs build passes and link checker is clean (no broken internal links).
- External reviewers (Docs lead + Support SME) sign off on the checklist doc for clarity and correctness.
implementation_notes:
Content alignment:
- Treat the checklist template as the canonical definition for step ordering + acceptance criteria.
- Use consistent terms across docs and Console: “API key”, “Project”, “Quota”, “Budget alerts”, “Model pinning”, “Fallback policy”, “Streaming”, “Retries/timeouts”.

Cross-language parity:
- Use a shared outline and verify each language quickstart contains the same conceptual steps; minor language-specific differences are OK but must be documented.
- Prefer linking from language quickstarts to a single “production readiness” guide rather than duplicating long explanations.

Known sensitive areas to be explicit about:
- Usage dashboard lag: add a callout (“usage can lag by X minutes; rely on response headers/logs for immediate verification”).
- Streaming disconnects: document reconnection patterns + recommended client configuration.
- 429 handling: document exponential backoff + respecting Retry-After where available.

Open questions to resolve in review:
- Exact phrasing for TTFS (“first successful 2xx”) and what counts as “production traffic” for TTFP; ensure docs do not over-promise metric definitions but remain accurate.
rollout_notes:
Docs and quickstarts should be ready prior to cohort rollout of the Console checklist.
- Behind-the-scenes: docs can be published broadly, but ensure Console deep links point to stable URLs.
- Coordinate timing with release notes so links in the release note land on final pages.
- Support enablement: share the final checklist doc + quickstart parity table with Support macros/triage playbook owners.
qa_plan:
Manual validation:
- Walkthrough for each language quickstart using a fresh test project:
  1) Create API key, set env var, run “first request”
  2) Enable streaming example and confirm disconnect guidance is discoverable
  3) Trigger a 401 (intentionally wrong key) and ensure troubleshooting section catches it quickly
  4) Trigger a 429 (lower quota in test project or run burst) and confirm docs point to proper backoff behavior
  5) Validate links to quota/budget pages + model pinning + fallback policy docs
  6) Confirm observability hooks section includes request_id correlation and where to view logs

Link validation:
- Run docs link checker; spot-check top inbound pages for redirects.

Review validation:
- Support SME reviews “common issues” sections for accuracy and usefulness (401/403, 429, streaming disconnect, usage lag).
